fields.v: TDAD (Test-Driven Agentic Development), pip package 'tdad', version Not stated; compared with a 'TDD Prompt' configuration (TDD procedural instructions, write tests first then implement) and a vanilla prompt

Code-test dependency graph (4 node types: File, Function, Class, Test; 5 edge types: CONTAINS, CALLS, IMPORTS, TESTS, INHERITS) built by AST parsing; static test map file test_map.txt (source file to test file, grep-able); SKILL.md, a 20-line skill definition (fix the bug, grep test_map.txt for related tests, run them and fix failures), simplified from 107 lines. TDD Prompt variant: procedural TDD instructions (119-line prompt). No specification document

Tool: Stage 1 indexing (AST parser, graph builder, test linker) and Stage 2 impact analysis (weighted strategies direct 0.95, transitive 0.70, coverage 0.80, imports 0.50; export test_map.txt). Agent: read issue, plan fix, implement, query test map for at-risk tests, verify tests, self-correct regressions, submit patch (Fig. 1)
Not stated (agents run autonomously; no human review in the flow)

fields.v: Tasks: SWE-bench Verified, 100 instances (Phase 1, first 100 in canonical order) and 25 (Phase 2, selected for diversity). Configurations: Phase 1 Vanilla vs TDD Prompt vs GraphRAG+TDD; Phase 2 Baseline vs TDAD Skill. Baseline: vanilla prompt (49 lines) / OpenCode without skill. Held constant within Phase 1: model Qwen3-Coder 30B Q4_K_M, llama.cpp, 32K context, temperature 0, 15-minute limit; Phase 2: model Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (MLX, 4-bit) and OpenCode v1.2.24, other settings not stated; both phases evaluated in the SWE-bench Docker harness. Configurations run sequentially. Acceptance tests: SWE-bench F2P and P2P tests. Repetitions: 1 run per configuration. Human intervention: none stated. Earlier ablations on prompt length (119 vs 49 lines) reported from prior experiments

fields.v: Phase 1: TDAD cut test-level regressions 6.08% to 1.82% (-70%; P2P failures 562 to 155, -72%; -81% vs TDD Prompt) with resolution 31% to 29% (-2 pp, more empty patches 26% vs 14%). TDD Prompt worse than vanilla (9.94%, +42% failures): 'TDD Prompting Paradox'. Instance-level regression rate higher for TDAD (33.3% vs 30.2%), explained as a denominator artifact (25 of 74 vs 26 of 86). Phase 2: resolution 24% to 32% (+8 pp), generation 40% to 68%. No significance tests

Distinguished configurations on regression rate in Phase 1 and on resolution/generation in Phase 2 (no regressions in Phase 2, so not on regressions). Repeatability: single run, temperature 0; two baseline resolutions lost in Phase 2 attributed to nondeterminism. Limitations stated: small samples without formal significance tests; sequential runs; auto-loop evaluation set risks overfitting; test-level regression weights all tests equally; P2P set may not cover all affected code

100 and 25 instances without significance tests; two small local models (frontier models may not show the paradox); Python only; static analysis misses dynamic dispatch and runtime code; auto-loop on 10 instances. Future: other languages via Tree-sitter, dynamic coverage, frontier models (Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4), composite resolution-regression metric
